slides.title: 5 dishwasher myths to drop before the holiday dishes

slides.fact: An efficient dishwasher can use about 4 gallons a load. Washing the same dishes by hand can take up to 27 gallons.

slides.myth: You have to rinse dishes before they go in.
slides.fact: Just scrape off the food. Pre-rinsing wastes water and can fool the soil sensor into running a lighter cycle.

slides.myth: You need the heated dry setting.
slides.fact: The heating element uses a lot of energy. The air-dry setting uses very little, so pick it when you can.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Energy Saver

slides.myth: Running it half full saves water and power.
slides.fact: A dishwasher uses about the same water and energy no matter how many dishes are inside. Wait for a full load.

slides.myth: A cast iron skillet can go in the dishwasher.
slides.fact: It strips the seasoning and invites rust. Lodge says to hand wash seasoned cast iron, dry it, and rub on a little oil.
